title: Ecosystems and food webs
examples: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
Can decomposers survive without living things around them?
Which part of an ecosystem is most important for recycling nutrients?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how energy moves in nature.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a food web. Look at the sun, the grass and the grasshopper. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Producers are organisms that make their own food using sunlight.
Consumers get energy by eating other living things for food.
Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into simpler substances.
Energy moves from the producers to the consumers in a food web.

items: Producers are eaten by primary consumers

explain.say: In a real pond ecosystem, sunlight powers the producers like reeds and pondweed.

draw.text: Pond food web: Sunlight powers life

faq.q: What is the main difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain shows one single path of energy transfer. A food web shows many interconnected feeding relationships in an ecosystem.
asks: Is a food web just a bunch of food chains?
How are food webs more accurate than food chains?

faq.q: Do decomposers need other living things to function?
faq.a: Decomposers break down dead matter, which is essential for recycling nutrients back into the soil for producers.
asks: What happens if there are no decomposers?

faq.q: Where does the energy in the ecosystem originally come from?
faq.a: Almost all energy in an ecosystem ultimately comes from the sun's energy, which producers capture.
asks: Is the sun the ultimate source of energy?
How does sunlight get into the food web?

faq.q: What are the primary consumers in a grassland ecosystem?
faq.a: Primary consumers are herbivores, meaning they eat only producers like grass and leaves.
asks: Give an example of a primary consumer.

faq.q: What is the role of omnivores in an ecosystem?
faq.a: Omnivores eat both plants and animals, which gives them flexibility in what they consume.
asks: Can an animal eat both things?

facts: Producers, like plants, use photosynthesis to convert light energy into chemical energy.
Consumers feed on other organisms to obtain the energy they need to survive.
Decomposers, such as bacteria and fungi, recycle nutrients from dead organic matter.
Energy flows through an ecosystem, moving from the sun to producers, then to consumers.

quiz.say: In a forest, grass is eaten by a rabbit, and the rabbit is eaten by a fox. This shows:
quiz.why: This single path shows one transfer of energy, which is a food chain.

wrong.0: A food web shows many interconnected paths, not just one line.
wrong.1: This describes the process of making food, not the energy transfer path.
wrong.2: This only describes what breaks down dead material, not the feeding relationship.

quiz.say: Which group of organisms breaks down dead leaves and wood?
quiz.why: Decomposers are specialized to break down complex organic matter back into soil nutrients.

wrong.0: Herbivores only eat plants, they do not break down all types of dead matter.
wrong.1: Carnivores eat other animals; decomposition is a different process.
wrong.3: Producers make food using sunlight; they do not primarily break down waste.

quiz.say: If a primary consumer eats only plants, it is called a:
quiz.why: Herbivores are defined by their diet of producers, like leaves and grass.

wrong.0: Producers are the ones making the food, not eating it.
wrong.2: Carnivores must eat other animals to survive.
wrong.3: Omnivores eat a mix of both plants and animals.
